verses.text: So Zeus spoke, and noble Cottus answered him:
“Mighty god, what you tell us is no mystery. We ourselves
know how far your wisdom and understanding surpass all others;
you have shielded the immortal gods from chilling ruin.
Thanks to your wise care, out of the misty darkness
and free of merciless chains, back once more
we have come, lord, son of Cronus, after suffering beyond imagining.
So now, with steady minds and careful planning,
we will defend your power in this terrible war,
fighting the Titans through the fiercest battles.”
So Cottus spoke. The gods, the givers of good things, approved
the words they heard, and their hearts longed for war
still more than before. They stirred up a dreadful battle,
all of them, female and male alike, on that day:
the Titan gods, all the children of Cronus,
and those Zeus had brought into the light from Erebus, the darkness beneath the earth,
terrifying, powerful beings with overwhelming strength.
A hundred hands sprang from the shoulders
of every one of them, and each had fifty heads
growing from his shoulders above his sturdy limbs.
These giants now faced the Titans in deadly battle,
holding towering rocks in their powerful hands.
Across from them, the Titans tightened their battle ranks
eagerly, and showed what their hands and strength could do,
as did their foes. The boundless sea roared terribly all around;
the earth crashed aloud, and the wide sky groaned
and shook. Tall Olympus shuddered from its base
under the immortals’ onslaught, and a heavy tremor reached
misty Tartarus, along with the piercing roar of feet
in the endless rush of battle, and the crash of mighty blows.
So they hurled their weapons of pain at one another.
The voices of both sides reached the starry sky
as they called out and clashed with a mighty battle shout.
Now Zeus no longer held back his fury;
at once his heart filled with rage, and he revealed
his full strength. From heaven and Olympus together
he advanced, flashing lightning without a pause. His thunderbolts
flew thick and fast with thunder and lightning
from his powerful hand, whirling sacred flame
in a ceaseless shower. All around, the life-giving earth roared
as it burned, and vast forests crackled loudly in the fire.
All the land boiled, and so did the streams of Oceanus
and the barren sea. Hot vapor wrapped around
the Titans beneath the earth, and flame reached the bright upper air,
boundless flame. Their eyes were blinded, strong as they were,
by the dazzling glare of thunderbolt and lightning.
An astonishing heat filled Chaos, the great chasm. To see it before you
with your own eyes and hear the sound with your own ears
was just as though Gaia, the Earth, and wide Ouranos, the Sky above,
were crashing together. Such a mighty roar would rise
if Earth were collapsing and Sky came crashing down from high above.
So great was the crash as the gods met in battle.
The winds roared amid the shaking and dust,
the thunder and lightning and smoking thunderbolts,
the weapons of great Zeus, and carried cries and shouts
between the two armies. An immense uproar rose
from that dreadful conflict, and their deeds revealed their strength.

uncertainties: Verse 659 is marked as textually doubtful in the supplied Greek; the overall sense of returning from darkness and release from chains is clear.
In verse 697, “beneath the earth” translates an epithet that can also mean “of the earth”; the Titans are taking part in the battle, so their precise location is uncertain.
